title: UV-Vis Spectrophotometric Quantification of Aqueous Copper(II) Ions
author: Marcus Vance, Optical Metrology Lab
abstract: The optical absorbance of aqueous copper(II) sulfate was evaluated across the range 0.010 M to 0.100 M at lambda_max = 635 nm. The system obeyed the Beer-Lambert law with linear correlation R^2 = 0.9997 and calculated molar absorptivity epsilon = 12.04 L/(mol·cm).
hypothesis: Absorbance of light through a homogeneous solution will be directly proportional to analyte concentration and path length without non-linear deviation below 0.15 M.
methodology: Serial dilutions prepared in 50 mL volumetric flasks. Standard 1.00 cm path length quartz cuvette loaded. Spectrophotometer zeroed against blank DI water at 635 nm.
observations: Clear blue color intensity increased monotonically with concentration. No precipitation or particulate scattering observed.
calculations: Linear regression: A = 12.04 * c + 0.002. At c = 0.050 M, measured A = 0.604 AU, transmittance %T = 24.89%. Calculated epsilon = 12.04 L/(mol·cm).
conclusion: The molar absorptivity was determined with high precision. The system serves as an exemplary calibration standard for unknown concentration assays.
